headline: South Asia: Cairo vows support for Riyadh as 2 Saudi officers killed in helicopter crash near Yemen
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Cairo vows support for Riyadh as 2 Saudi officers killed in helicopter crash near Yemen.
- Western Russia: Russian airstrikes on Sloviansk kill six, injure 15, people trapped under rubble – photos.
- India: Ukraine Fires 1,000 Drones At Russia, St Petersburg Oil Sites Ablaze.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Army’s 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: US Army’s 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated.
The Army's 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated as the service reshapes its PSYOP and information warfare forces to counter global adversaries.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
The Caribbean: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russian airstrikes on Sloviansk kill six, injure 15, people trapped under rubble – photos.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: Russian airstrikes on Sloviansk kill six, injure 15, people trapped under rubble – photos.
Russian aerial bombs and drones killed six people and injured 15 in Sloviansk on 17 October, damaging over 20 houses; rescue workers are recovering bodies.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: University lecturer Kostiantyn Chub killed in Russian attack on Poltava.
Poltava Pedagogical University lecturer Kostiantyn Chub has been killed in a Russian drone attack that targeted residential areas in Poltava.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Warehouse catches fire in Lviv due to Russian drone attack.
A Russian drone attack has damaged a logistics complex and caused a warehouse fire in Malekhiv, while drone debris damaged homes in Murovane.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Zelenskyy speaks with Trump envoys.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has held talks with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, discussing Florida team meetings, ongoing Russian strikes and air defence needs.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Ukraine strikes oil facility in St. Petersburg as part of ‘massive’ drone attack.
- Politico Europe, The Moscow Times, 7 hours ago: Ukraine strikes oil facility in St. Petersburg as part of ‘massive’ drone attack.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said last week he had ordered the resumption of strikes on Russian oil refineries following a three-day pause.
- Politico Europe, 4 hours ago: France says Israel must ‘stop these acts of terror’ following attack on EU diplomats.
Video footage of the incident in Taybeh, north of Jerusalem, showed settlers confronting a convoy of diplomats.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Sudanese gold miners describe deadly airstrike that killed 72.
- Africanews, 9 hours ago: Sudanese gold miners describe deadly airstrike that killed 72.
Sudanese miners injured in a deadly airstrike along the border with Egypt last week have been describing how the incident unfolded.
- Africanews, 8 hours ago: Nigeria's Army Chief of Staff visits troops in Borno after deaths of 15 soliders.
The Nigerian Army Chief of Staff is visiting troops stationed in the northeast of the country, a few days after jihadists killed fifteen soldiers in the region.
- Africanews, 11 hours ago: DRC accuses ex-president Kabila of planning 'general attack' on the country.
Officials in DR Congo are accusing former president Joseph Kabila of planning a general attack on the country. Kabila on Monday joined forces with the rebel M23 to head a new outfit , taking a more direct role in the insurgency ravaging eastern DRC.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Bereaved families seek criminal probe of Netanyahu over October 7 account.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Bereaved families seek criminal probe of Netanyahu over October 7 account.
The families also seek scrutiny of his account of Qatari funding diverted to Hamas’s military wing and his handling of warnings before the attack.
- Jerusalem Post, 6 hours ago: 'You are the real target': Netanyahu warns Iran developing ICBMs, nuclear weapons to target US.
Netanyahu told FOX News that, if reelected prime minister, his key objectives would be to end the threat posed by Iran, expand the Abraham Accords, and seize the future of AI development.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Democrats' Golan, Kariv decry gov't inaction on West Bank violence in visit to wounded journalist.
Democrats leader Golan and MK Kariv visited Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine after she was attacked in the West Bank, accusing the government of failing to address Jewish extremist violence.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: Sudan army accused of drone strike on livestock market.
Sudan’s army says it struck RSF command centres in South Darfur, but the RSF says a crowded livestock market was hit.
South Africa: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Cairo vows support for Riyadh as 2 Saudi officers killed in helicopter crash near Yemen.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, 2 hours ago: Cairo vows support for Riyadh as 2 Saudi officers killed in helicopter crash near Yemen.
Egypt is ready to provide Saudi Arabia with the support it needs to defend its security and stability, the presidency said on Sunday. Earlier in the day, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said two officers were killed when their helicopter crashed near the Yemen border, after the rebel group claimed it shot the aircraft down. The coalition blamed a “technical malfunction” for the helicopter crash, which inflicted its first military fatalities since the long-running conflict with the Houthis reignited in July.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Times of India - Top Stories, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 5 hours ago: Egypt ‘ready to defend’ Saudi Arabia against Houthis.
• President Sisi says Cairo will take ‘any measure’ to protect kingdom if asked • Iran backs ‘political process’, offers to mediate • Saudi, Houthi forces trade fire CAIRO: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi pledged on Saturday that Egypt was ready to help defend Saudi Arabia against attacks by Yemen’s Houthi forces if requested, as fighting intensified across the region and Cairo moved towards possible parliamentary authorisation for support.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: 8 India-sponsored terrorists killed in Quetta, Khuzdar, Nushki districts: ISPR.
Security forces have killed eight “India-sponsored” terrorists during three intelligence-based operations conducted in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts of Balochistan, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Sunday. The IBOs took place on Oct 17 (Saturday) on the “reported presence of terrorists belonging to Indian proxy Fitna al Hindustan”, the military’s media affairs wing said in its press release. The state has designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al Hindustan to highlight India’s role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.
- The Hindu - International, Africanews, Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Drone strikes in the Black Sea raise fears of Russian escalation to test NATO's response.
The attacks in the two countries' exclusive economic zones threaten a global shipping route and have left two people dead, with at least 25 still missing. They also run the risk of drawing other countries directly into the war for Ukraine
India - bottom line: Ukraine Fires 1,000 Drones At Russia, St Petersburg Oil Sites Ablaze.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 6 hours ago: Ukraine Fires 1,000 Drones At Russia, St Petersburg Oil Sites Ablaze.
The attack comes amid deepening tensions between Ukraine and Washington, with U.S. President Donald Trump criticizing Kyiv for its strikes on Russian oil infrastructure.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Manipur in turmoil again: 15 houses torched; 1 killed, several injured in gun attack.
In Chassad village, located in Manipur's Kamjong district, at least 15 houses were burned late Saturday night. Suspected militants attacked the village, causing significant chaos and civilians to flee for safety. A Kuki civilian was killed during the assault, and four others suffered injuries from gunfire. Deputy Chief Minister Nemcha Kipgen condemned the violence and called for strict action against the perpetrators.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 6 hours ago: Russia sold Alaska for peanuts. Now it guards America against Moscow.
In 1867, Russia sold Alaska to the United States for $7.2 million, reflecting strategic concerns. The decision stemmed from fears of potential conflict with Britain during the Crimean War. Subsequent discoveries of natural resources transformed Alaska's economic importance significantly over the years. Alaska emerged as a crucial military platform for the United States against the Russian Far East.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 6 hours ago: Iran offers to reopen Strait of Hormuz in seven days if US accepts conditions.
Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araqchi reiterated that the proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz remains in place. Tehran is analyzing the US response regarding its conditions for ending the conflict. These conditions include lifting sanctions and ending aggression in the region. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump expressed optimism about a swift resolution to the war and lower gas prices.
Asia - bottom line: US-Russia deal, Trump-Zelensky clash could leave Ukraine out in the cold.
- South China Morning Post - China, 16 hours ago: US-Russia deal, Trump-Zelensky clash could leave Ukraine out in the cold.
From US threats to cut off intelligence support for Ukraine to a waiver of tariffs on Russian ⁠exports and a diesel deal that could help Russia fund its war, it has been a damaging week for ties between Kyiv and its most important ally, Washington. US President Donald Trump, frustrated by high energy costs he blames partly on Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries, has repeatedly criticised Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Palau authorities are investigating an alleged underwater attack by a South Korean divemaster on Taiwanese musician Devon Song and his Bangladeshi divemaster. Song, a member of the music group Nan Quan Mama, posted on social media that he and his divemaster, Sobuj Patwary, were attacked by a South Korean divemaster known as “Romeo”. - South China Morning Post - China, 16 hours ago: How land power could help US forces counter China in the Indo-Pacific.
Senior US commanders have highlighted the importance of land-based troops and equipment stationed in the Asia-Pacific in any conflict with China, countering assumptions that such a war would be fought mainly at sea and in the air. General Ron Clark, commander of US Army Pacific, said the “tyranny of distance” made it difficult to rely on air and naval forces during a panel discussion at the Association of the United States Army’s annual meeting this week. The comments reflect mounting concerns...
- South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: Lithuanians take shelter, Nato jets scramble as suspected drone explodes.
A suspected drone exploded over Lithuania ⁠after triggering an alert that forced residents in northern and central areas to seek shelter for an hour on Sunday morning, the president and other defence officials said. Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry said later it regretted the incident in Lithuania’s airspace, adding that it may have resulted from Russian ‌electronic warfare diverting drones off course. Scott Boland strikes twice in two balls during a brief period of play as rain almost entirely washes out the first day of the second Test between Australia and South Africa Gqeberha.
